extracted.intended_audience: public-interest advocates, NGO lawyers, and technical experts preparing comments on EPA (and similar) rulemakings
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for drafting notice-and-comment submissions that counter industry influence in agency rulemaking, emphasizing pre-proposal engagement, technical depth, record-building, and follow-up availability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engage with pre-proposal exchanges
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the comment engage with pre-proposal exchanges between agency and industry (FOIA, records of meetings)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pre-proposal engagement is where the rule is built; industry enjoys a large advantage in pre-proposal contacts. Commenters should seek and rely on FOIA-obtained records of meetings and other pre-proposal communications, file petitions for rulemaking, submit ANPRM responses, organize sign-on letters from technical experts, and pursue direct meetings with rule writers during the pre-proposal period to place public-interest positions into the record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide public-interest counter-data of comparable technical depth
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the comment provide public-interest counter-data of comparable technical depth to industry submissions?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Industry engages in many informal, technical exchanges (dozens per rule); public-interest comments should aspire to similar substantive depth by providing original research, empirical data, modeling, and detailed analyses. Include methods, data sources, and clear technical argumentation so agency staff can rely on and verify the material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify which agency assumptions originated with industry
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the comment identify which agency assumptions originated with industry?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare proposed rule language and underlying assumptions to industry pre-proposal positions and submissions. Flag where agency assumptions or framing mirror industry inputs, and note absence of independent justification. Explicitly trace assumptions back to industry sources when possible to show lack of independent agency analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make available follow-up technical engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the comment make available follow-up technical engagement (expert availability, modeling support)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beyond submitting documents, offer concrete follow-up: make experts available for meetings, offer modeling or analytic support, provide contact points for clarification, and be prepared for repeated substantive touches to mirror industry’s sustained technical engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Build a record on the asymmetry of stakeholder engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the comment build a record on the asymmetry of stakeholder engagement?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly document on the record that key data or positions relied on by the agency originated with industry, demand disclosure of pre-proposal communications, and call for parallel public-interest input. Building this record supports later judicial review (hard-look review) and highlights stakeholder imbalance.
